sources: Al Jazeera video newsfeed 'Mass rally against Netanyahu ahead of pivotal Israeli election'; Geo News rally report; Ynetnews campaign coverage
fault_line: Accountability or a harder line? The Tel Aviv crowds demand an Oct 7 inquiry Netanyahu refuses -- while commenters argue the protesters want him gone for being too soft, not too harsh.

sections.what_happened: Thousands (tens of thousands per VidiaNews/TRT aerial footage) rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday evening in the final large protest against PM Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Tuesday Oct 27's election, described as the most consequential in Israel's history. The crowd, organised by the October Council (families of Oct 7 victims/hostages), demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures behind the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023 attacks -- an inquiry Netanyahu has refused. Chief rival Gadi Eisenkot attended, as did Lapid, Liberman and Golan. Pre-blackout polls: KAN projects 52 seats for Eisenkot's bloc vs 50 for Netanyahu's in the 120-seat Knesset, neither at the 61 needed. Netanyahu simultaneously campaigned in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market urging a Likud ('Mahal') vote.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) + Geo News (T3, via registry 'Dawn / Geo News'). Business Standard carries the same rally but has NO declared tier and does NOT count. Ynetnews (T3) corroborates the campaign context (deadlock, <100 hours framing).
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu's camp frames the election as a security choice, not an accountability vote: his Jerusalem market rally leaned on Iranian-flag imagery and 'enemies want to destroy us' messaging, and his Saturday video (see 0700-03) calls the week 'fateful'. Social comment threads split on whether the protest is about Oct 7 accountability or about Netanyahu being 'too soft' -- the rally's meaning is contested even among its opponents' critics. Polls are pre-blackout projections, not results.
sections.why_matters: Tens of thousands filled Tel Aviv against Netanyahu three days before the vote -- demanding the Oct 7 inquiry he refuses -- while the polls say neither side can reach 61. The most consequential election in Israel's history is now a turnout war.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (in-window publication) -- Final mass anti-Netanyahu rally in Tel Aviv ahead of Israel's Oct 27 election; Eisenkot attends; polls deadlocked below a majority
